correctness.rationale: With one point fixed, the only possible second-point atomic relations are equality, strict earlier/later, or distinct and tied. Matching the set of realizable availability triples is thus necessary and sufficient in a two-move game, including reversal of spoiler direction after round one. The typical profile includes both kinds of interior blocks, and the only residual choices are endpoint singleton indicators. The displayed singleton endpoint tests are rank two and their Boolean combinations select all four states independently. The labelled block sequence EGF is 1/(2−e^z); subtracting 1/[2(ρ−z)] makes it holomorphic through any fixed-radius disk of radius R between 1 and the next pole modulus. Thus c_n=1/(2ρ^(n+1))+O(R^(−n)), and the exact endpoint singleton probabilities c_(n−1)/c_n and c_(n−2)/c_n (both endpoints distinct for the second count at n≥2) give Bernoulli(ρ) limiting endpoint bits with error o(ρ^n). The no-interior-nonsingleton obstruction has EGF 1+A+A²/(1−z) with A=e^z−1, including zero and one block once each. Its nth coefficient tends to (e−1)^2 by absolute summability at 1. The analogous missing-singleton-interior EGF has denominator 1−(e^z−1−z); since e−2<1 its coefficients decay on some circle of radius greater than one. This proves the O(ρ^n) typical-event and probability error bounds. Four endpoint atoms, with equal middle masses, give the displayed 2×3×2 choices. Their polynomials are injectively parametrized (compare constant, linear and quadratic coefficients), and Hermite–Lindemann precludes a nonzero difference vanishing at ρ. The rank-two witness H recognizes exactly the first obstruction's complement, so its strictly positive leading term 2ρ(e−1)^2 makes any smaller exponential base impossible; rank one cannot distinguish any nonempty model. I inspected checker.py without executing it; it checks finite profiles, weighted enumeration and obstruction coefficients but not analytic error bounds. Those bounds follow from the proof.

originality.rationale: The October 26 Resultary theorem on exactly the same measure and signature already gives all-FO exponential convergence, the limit field, and an effective formula. Cameron–Kang–Stark already give the enumerator and relevant block statistics. Pass is restricted to the explicit rank-two spectrum and sharp convergence scale: the earlier formula leaves a finite type monoid and its projection to be resolved and the earlier analytic proof gives an unspecified radius greater than ρ, not the rank-two threshold at 1. The new work identifies all the recurrent endpoint states, isolates the atypical logical profile producing the pole at 1, and computes its positive sharpness constant. It is not new qualitative convergence or just plugging an integer into an earlier rate formula.
